newsitem.title: USA: Calif. governor steps up flood recovery efforts.
newsitem.headline: Calif. governor steps up flood recovery efforts.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson announced steps on Thursday to help hard-hit areas clean up after last month's floods.

Wilson directed his office of emergency services to provide $8.25 million in immediate disaster relief to damaged areas. The money will help cash-strapped counties where resources have been severely depleted by the storm's damage.

The $8.25 million will be used to cover emergency repair and debris removal costs incurred by local governments. The office of emergency services will immediately begin issuing the funds, the Republican governor said.
The governor also ordered the department of water resources to immediately begin pumping out standing water on over 70,000 acres of land to save and protect premanent crops that are still submerged.

"Even today, several feet of standing water remain in some of our richest farmland, drowning crops, threatening thousands of acres of orchards and vineyards, and eroding the banks of levees," Wilson said in a statement.
The January storms flooded thousands of homes and businesses and inundated tens of thousands of acres of farmland in northern and central California.

The governor has declared states of emergency in 48 counties. Damage in California from the January storms has been estimated at over $1.5 billion. Flood and rain damage to state agriculture alone was estimated at $245 million.
